executive_summary: Green hydrogen electrolyzers present a monitor-and-wait opportunity, not an immediate investment. Section 45V tax credits created a 2027 construction deadline that triggered both genuine project momentum and forced market selection, but major cancellations by Air Products and BP in 2025 demonstrate that subsidy-dependent economics remain fragile. Real-world electrolyzer costs running 60-300% above published projections and only 10% of announced 2030 capacity having identified buyers indicate the sector is still working through fundamental commercial viability questions. Active monitoring makes sense given large projects reaching FID and substantial venture capital flowing to efficiency-focused new entrants, but capital deployment should wait for clearer evidence that projects can pencil without maximum subsidy support.

market_shifts.description: U.S. Treasury and IRS released final rules for Section 45V Clean Hydrogen Production Tax Credit on January 3, 2025, offering up to $3.00/kg as a 10-year incentive, but revised law in mid-2025 limited eligibility to facilities beginning construction before end of 2027.

Major project cancellations occurred in 2025-2026: Air Products exited three U.S. projects including a $500M Massena plant in February 2025 after regulatory changes made existing hydroelectric power ineligible for tax credits, and BP cancelled the 1.5 GW Duqm project in Oman in December 2025.

Three large-scale green hydrogen projects reached Final Investment Decision in 2026: Orica's Hunter Valley Hub (50 MW, largest Australian renewable hydrogen project), the Barrow project (30 MW), and movement toward FEED for Hy2gen's 275 MW Courant project.

PEM electrolyzer capital costs fell from roughly $1,200-$1,500/kW in 2020 to approximately $700-$1,000/kW by 2026, though real-world 2024 system costs averaging $3,000/kW suggest actual costs remain 60-300% higher than commonly cited projections.

First major long-term offtake agreement signed in March 2025 between RWE and TotalEnergies for 30,000 metric tons/year over 15 years, while only 10% of announced capacity planned by 2030 has identified buyers despite 255 developers actively negotiating agreements.

incumbents.name: Plug Power
incumbents.differentiation: Secured three major electrolyzer supply contracts in 2026, including the largest Australian renewable hydrogen project (50 MW Hunter Valley), a 30 MW Barrow project, and a 275 MW FEED contract for Hy2gen's Courant ammonium nitrate decarbonization project.

incumbents.name: John Cockerill Hydrogen
incumbents.differentiation: Entered U.S. market with a Baytown, Texas alkaline electrolyzer gigafactory awarded $34M in DOE tax credits, designed for 1 GW/year manufacturing capacity and 200 new jobs.

new_entrants.name: Electric Hydrogen
new_entrants.differentiation: Raised $380M in an oversubscribed Series C in October 2023, bringing total funding to approximately $600M from investors including Energy Impact Partners, Fifth Wall, and Fortescue.

new_entrants.name: Hysata
new_entrants.differentiation: Achieved 95% system efficiency at commercial scale with capillary-fed electrolyser technology versus roughly 75% for existing commercial electrolysers, confirmed in peer-reviewed research showing 39.4-41.6 kWh/kg H2 at 0.8 A/cm².

recommendations.text: Track Section 45V utilization and project execution through the December 2027 construction deadline to assess whether tax credit economics can translate announced projects into operating assets, with the risk that the deadline creates artificial urgency followed by a funding cliff rather than genuine commercial momentum. The spread between Air Products cancelling projects when regulatory changes eliminated subsidy eligibility and three large projects reaching FID in 2026 suggests the tax credit is necessary but may not be sufficient for project viability.

Follow Hysata's commercialization trajectory and any efficiency validation by third-party projects, given that 95% system efficiency versus 75% incumbent performance represents the kind of step-change that could alter unit economics if it scales beyond pilot, with the technical risk that capillary-fed electrolysis faces durability or manufacturing challenges not visible in lab demonstrations. A $111M Series B in May 2024 and peer-reviewed Nature Communications validation provide credibility, but efficiency advantages proven at small scale often fail to survive manufacturing reality.

Defer active deal sourcing in electrolyzer manufacturers until offtake contract penetration rises meaningfully above the current 10% of announced 2030 capacity, because capital equipment suppliers face existential demand risk when their customers cannot secure buyers. The gap between 255 developers negotiating offtake agreements and only 10% of capacity having identified buyers indicates the hydrogen market is still hunting for its demand base, and electrolyzer manufacturers cannot outrun that uncertainty regardless of their technology or balance sheet.

Watch for clarity on real-world installed system costs through 2027, given that published projections of $700-$1,000/kW clash with reported 2024 averages of $3,000/kW, because cost assumptions underpin every production economics model and a persistent 60-300% gap between forecast and reality makes current project pro formas unreliable for investment decisions. DOE targets of $2/kg by 2026 and $1/kg by 2031 become unachievable if the denominator is wrong by a factor of two, regardless of subsidy support.

all_claims.claim: Electric Hydrogen (EH2) raised $380 million in an oversubscribed Series C round announced October 3, 2023, bringing its total funding to roughly $600 million.
As of a July 2026 company profile, Electric Hydrogen has raised $603M in total funding from investors including Energy Impact Partners, Fifth Wall, and Fortescue.
Green hydrogen startup Hysata raised $111 million in a Series B round announced May 9, 2024.
Hysata's capillary-fed electrolyser (CFE) technology has achieved 95% system efficiency, confirmed at commercial scale, versus roughly 75% efficiency for existing commercial electrolysers.
A peer-reviewed 2022 Nature Communications paper reported Hysata's capillary-fed electrolysis cell achieving 95% (HHV) energy efficiency at 0.8 A/cm² and 85°C, equating to 39.4–41.6 kWh per kg of H2.
John Cockerill Hydrogen entered the U.S. market by acquiring manufacturing space in Baytown, Texas to build a new electrolyzer gigafactory.

John Cockerill Hydrogen was awarded $34 million in U.S. Department of Energy tax credits for its Baytown Gigafactory project, out of $42 billion in total funding requests submitted for that DOE allocation round.
The Baytown, Texas John Cockerill facility is expected to create 200 new jobs and produce 1 GW per year of alkaline electrolyzer manufacturing capacity.
The U.S. Treasury and IRS released final rules for the Section 45V Clean Hydrogen Production Tax Credit on January 3, 2025, offering up to $3.00 per kilogram of clean hydrogen as a 10-year incentive.
Under a revised U.S. law passed in mid-2025, only clean hydrogen facilities that begin construction before the end of 2027 remain eligible to receive the Section 45V tax credit.
The U.S. DOE's technical target for PEM electrolysis is $2/kg for clean hydrogen production by 2026, with a longer-term goal of $1/kg by 2031.
PEM electrolyzer CAPEX fell from roughly $1,200–$1,500 per kW in 2020 to approximately $700–$1,000 per kW by 2026, according to H2Pro.

A 2024 industry review (cited via LinkedIn analysis of Fletcher's data) found real-world 2024 electrolyzer system costs averaging $3,000/kW, far higher than a commonly cited CSIRO assumption of $1,800/kW — indicating electrolysis costs have historically been underestimated by 60% to 300%.

RWE and TotalEnergies signed a long-term (15-year) offtake agreement announced March 12, 2025, under which TotalEnergies will purchase approximately 30,000 metric tons of green hydrogen per year from RWE for its Leuna, Germany refinery.

Plug Power was selected in April 2026 to supply a 275 MW GenEco electrolyzer system under a Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) contract for Hy2gen's Courant decarbonized ammonium nitrate project in Baie-Comeau, Québec, Canada.

Plug Power won a 50 MW electrolyzer order (announced July 7, 2026) as Orica's Hunter Valley Hub in Australia became the largest Australian renewable hydrogen project to reach Final Investment Decision.
The 30 MW Barrow Green Hydrogen Project reached Final Investment Decision on May 20, 2026, with Plug Power supplying 30 MW of its GenEco PEM electrolyzers.
As of September 2024, 255 hydrogen project developers were actively negotiating offtake agreements with buyers or had already signed them, per Wood Mackenzie.

Of all clean hydrogen production capacity planned globally by 2030, only about 10% of announced projects have identified a buyer, according to BloombergNEF research cited by the Green Hydrogen Organisation.

Air Products announced on February 24, 2025 that it would exit three U.S.-based projects, including canceling its planned $500 million liquid green hydrogen plant in Massena, New York, because recent regulatory developments rendered its existing hydroelectric power supply ineligible for the hydrogen production tax credit.
The Massena, New York plant that Air Products cancelled was designed to produce 35 tons per day of green hydrogen.
BP cancelled the gigascale 1.5 GW Duqm Green Hydrogen Project in Oman in December 2025, which had been designed to produce 150,000 tonnes of hydrogen annually.
Developers of green hydrogen projects have scaled back investments and scrapped projects globally due to elevated production costs and weak demand, according to Reuters reporting from July 23, 2025.
